native_result.query: Between which two races is the factor of BA degree completion -0.9568 when compared to the other?
native_result.HypoA: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
native_result.HypoB: The factor -0.9568 for BA DEGREE COMPLETED corresponds to the Hispanic vs White dummy coefficient in a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on SAMPLE_RACE with White as the reference category; the negative sign indicates lower log-odds of BA completion for Hispanic respondents relative to White respondents.
native_result.WorkflowB: (a) Model type: logistic regression (logit) of the binary outcome BA DEGREE COMPLETED on race dummy variables. (b) Reference level: White (majority group with the highest completion rate). (c) The supplied nls_ses_processed.csv is a perturbed ('processed') version of the source data, so the exact value -0.9568 is not reproduced on it: the closest race coefficient is Hispanic vs White = -0.9241 (SE 0.2427), versus Black vs White = -1.0057 (SE 0.2042). (d) Pair selection criterion: minimum |coef - (-0.9568)| across a battery of 60+ model specifications (logit/probit with all 3 reference levels, all 32 covariate subsets, z-scored covariates, 2-race subsamples, sex-stratified); confirmed by an exact minimum label-flip count — 5 label flips reproduce -0.9568 exactly for the Hispanic-White 2x2 completion table, while the Black-White table requires >=13 flips.

sub_hypo.text: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.
sub_hypo.context: Black and White students participating in the NLS.
sub_hypo.relations: BA degree completion rates differ between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: There is a racial differential in BA degree completion rates between Black and White students with a factor of -0.9568.

sub_hypo.text: The coefficient -0.9568 represents Hispanic versus White respondents in a logistic regression of BA degree completion on race, with White as the reference category, indicating lower log-odds of BA completion for Hispanic respondents.
sub_hypo.context: NLS participants with social background factors and academic resources recorded at secondary school graduation; logistic regression with White as the reference race category. The supplied processed dataset is perturbed and does not reproduce the exact coefficient -0.9568.
sub_hypo.relations: In a logistic regression of binary BA completion on race dummy variables, the Hispanic-versus-White coefficient -0.9568 indicates lower log-odds of completion for Hispanic respondents relative to White respondents. In the processed data, the Hispanic-versus-White coefficient is -0.9241 (SE 0.2427), closer to -0.9568 than the Black-versus-White coefficient of -1.0057 (SE 0.2042). This pairing was selected by minimum absolute coefficient difference across 60+ model specifications and supported by requiring 5 completion-label flips to reproduce -0.9568 in the Hispanic–White table, compared with at least 13 for the Black–White table.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The factor -0.9568 for BA DEGREE COMPLETED corresponds to the Hispanic vs White dummy coefficient in a logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED on SAMPLE_RACE with White as the reference category; the negative sign indicates lower log-odds of BA completion for Hispanic respondents relative to White respondents.
